Critically, these controls reach far beyond U.S. borders. Through the expansive Foreign Direct Product Rule (FDPR), the regulations capture certain foreign-made products if they are based on U.S. technology or software. This powerful rule asserts U.S. jurisdiction over a foreign-made chip if its design uses American software (like EDA tools) or if it’s produced with U.S.-origin manufacturing equipment.
